event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description:
“Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.”

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

Topics include:

  • Gesture drawing fundamentals

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective

  • Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution

  • Differentiating core and cast shadows

  • Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy

Whether you’re just starting or refining your figure drawing skills, Francesco’s instruction will help you grow with clarity and confidence.

Supplies Needed:

* 2 Charcoal pencils 2B
* 1 White plastic eraser
* 1 Kneaded eraser
* 1 18″x 24″ Newsprint pad – 100 sheet
* Blending stumps assorted sizes 4 pc.
* No oils, solvent or fixatives are allowed in the class

Passage: A Themed Members Show

We invite all Alliance member artists to submit one original work inspired by the theme “Passage” for exhibition in the main gallery during October 2026. The theme encourages both literal and abstract interpretations of transition, movement, transformation, and emotional or psychological change, from shifting seasons and aging to journeys through physical and symbolic spaces. Artists are also encouraged to explore unconventional approaches, including text-based works and mixed media incorporating poetry, prose, or fragmented narratives, while defining the theme through their own unique perspective.

Submit Online (artinlee.org/passage): September 13th by 11:59 PM
Call Details: Passage – Call Prospectus

 

_____________________________________________________________

Foulds Theater Gallery

Time no Time
by Dahye Kim

Ambiguous, intangible, and in flux, Dahye Kim’s installation explores time and memory as processes of becoming, dissolving, and re-emerging. Time no Time, her second solo exhibition in Florida, reflects on a reality increasingly mediated and reduced through technology and the online world. Drawn from photographs taken during her travels and thoughts developed over the past six years across diverse natural landscapes in the United States, the exhibition examines shifting perceptions of presence, memory, and temporality in digital space.

As a conceptual digital media artist, Kim creates immersive environments using video, photography, internet, coding, light, and sound. Her practice investigates the intersections of time, memory, environment, and scientific ideas through technologically mediated experiences. In this exhibition, reflective screens function as temporal mirrors in which past, present, and future collapse into a continuous surface.

Transforming the gallery into a fluid and shifting environment, Kim blurs the boundaries between material and immaterial, presence and illusion, and the natural and artificial. Minimal gestures—subtle color transitions, horizon-like lines, and shifting light—evoke unstable landscapes suspended between physical and virtual space. Her work gestures toward the evolving condition of the internet, where time fragments, loops, and becomes increasingly abstract. Through minimal digital interventions, Kim invites viewers to experience time not as linear, but as something sensed, elusive, and constantly unfolding.

More on the artist: dahyekim.com

 

_____________________________________________________________

Member Gallery

Selected Works by Marian Fuller

Marian Fuller’s mixed-media exhibition focuses on the beauty hidden within everyday life by transforming found and recycled materials into richly textured works that invite the viewer into a state of discovery. Inspired by neighborhood walks, international travel, thrift stores, and overlooked objects, she creates compositions that encourage viewers to look beyond the familiar and uncover unexpected meaning in ordinary things.

Working with handmade paper, reclaimed materials, shredded credit cards, and other found objects, Fuller embraces experimentation and sustainability, allowing each piece to tell its own story through texture and layered details. Visitors are encouraged to experience the work up close, exploring the materials and subtle surprises woven throughout the collection while discovering the joy and adventure that define her creative process.

Featured Artwork: “Corinthian Highway” by Kellen Beck Mills, “Time no Time” Digital Art by Dahye Kim (2020-2026) & “Item-7.13” by Marian Fuller

event.title: Autumn Magic: Witch’s Hat Wreath
event.description:
Get into the Halloween spirit by creating a whimsical Witch’s Hat Wreath that’s sure to cast a spell on your front door! event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description:
Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter.

Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings.

By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently.

For the first 2 classes, we will be limiting our palette to black and white.

event.title: A Ghost Class- Sculpting with Jeff Ocasio
event.description:
Gather with us for a ghostly afternoon of creativity as you sculpt your own friendly ghost. This class welcomes artists of all skill levels, whether you’re a beginner excited to explore your creative side or an experienced artist wanting to experiment with a new medium. Led by Jeff, whose relaxed and conversational teaching style encourages individual creativity, you’ll learn how to layer and manipulate masking tape using paper, wire, and glass marbles for the eyes to build a sturdy, free-standing ghost approximately 7 inches tall. At the end of class, you’ll take home your one-of-a-kind masking tape sculpture along with an instructional handout to help you seal and paint your artwork at home using easy-to-find materials.

The class begins with a short tour of the artists’ studios inside DAAS CO-OP Gallery and The Union Artist Studios at the Arts & Eats Café.

All supplies provided

event.title: Drawing Fundamentals (Ages 16+)
event.description:
Discover the joy of drawing in this inspiring 7-week course designed for artists of every skill level. Whether you’re a complete beginner who thinks you can’t draw or an experienced artist looking to refresh your skills and see your work in a new way, this class offers a supportive and engaging environment to grow.

Through guided exercises and personalized instruction, students will build confidence while developing essential drawing techniques, including observation, proportion, composition, value, and line quality. Working from a variety of subjects—including still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin drawing what is actually in front of you. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation of accurate, expressive, and confident drawing.

By the end of the seven weeks, you’ll have a stronger understanding of the fundamentals, improved observational skills, and the confidence to continue your artistic journey with a fresh perspective.

Supplies:

  • 2 Charcoal Pencils, 6B extra soft
  • 2 White charcoal pencils OR White Compressed Charcoal
  • Pencil sharpener
  • Kneaded eraser

Paper provided

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet
event.description:
In this fun and relaxed four-week series, you’ll discover the building blocks of crochet while creating a beginner-friendly fall pumpkin. This class is designed for anyone who has wanted to learn to crochet, no prior experience required.

We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together.

Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own.

Supplies needed:

  • 5mm or 5.5mm crochet hook
  • Medium weight acrylic yarn
    • Body: orange, rust, cream, and other lighter fall themed colors (pick one)
    • Stem: brown and green (pick one)

event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description:
You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter?

With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work.

Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections.

We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results.

This class is designed for everyone from the weekend photographer looking to sharpen their skills to semi-professional photographers and local realtors who want to create more polished, compelling images for their work.

Bring your questions and curiosity and leave with new tools and techniques to take your photography to the next level.

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet

We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together.

Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own.

Supplies needed:

  • 5mm or 5.5mm crochet hook
  • Medium weight acrylic yarn

Unlock your creativity in this engaging weekly painting class with beloved artist and instructor, Terry Lynn Spry! Designed for all skill levels—from beginners to seasoned professionals—this class allows students to work at their own pace with their preferred subject and medium.

event.title: He Said, She Said: Writing Better Dialogue
event.description:
Bad dialog is one of the surest signs of an amateur writer. In this course taught by award-winning novelist Roberto Calas, you’ll learn the subtle secrets of making the spoken word sing. Or written words that are spoken, sing. You get the point. Either way, readers will sing your praises with these helpful tips on dialog.

We’ll take a deep dive into the world of character speech, covering a comprehensive array of categories including:

  • Intrinsic vs. Extrinsic
  • High Tension vs. Low Tension
  • What lies beneath – Underspeak
  • Characterization Through Dialog
  • Slang and Jargon
  • Expressive Lengthening
  • Keep or Cut
  • Dialog Tags

event.title: Mend & Make New
event.description: Mend & Make New is a six‑week creative repair course that teaches students how to refresh, reinforce, and reimagine their clothing using both subtle and expressive techniques. Through invisible mending, visible patchwork, embroidery, darning, and hybrid redesign, students learn how to assess damage, choose the right materials, and build repairs that are both durable and personal. The class blends practical skill‑building with organic, discovery‑based learning while encouraging students to explore materials, experiment with stitches, and find their own style of repair. event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description:
You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter?

With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work.

Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections.

We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results.

The Quill at Alliance for the Arts is a writers group with the goal of building a stronger creative writing community in Southwest Florida. event.title: Alliance Morning Market
event.description:
The Alliance for the Arts has reimagined its community market experience with the launch of the Alliance Morning Artisan Market, a new monthly event held on the third Saturday of each month from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. The shift moves the Alliance’s former Wednesday night market to a vibrant Saturday morning gathering designed to bring families, artists, and the community together for a full day of creativity and connection.

The first Alliance Morning Market will take place Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026, on the Alliance’s 10-acre campus at 10091 McGregor Blvd. The market will feature a curated mix of artisans and vendors, local artists, and live entertainment, creating a welcoming, festival-style atmosphere for all ages.

By moving the market to Saturdays, the Alliance is aligning it with two popular free programs already offered on campus: Free Family ArtLabs, held from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., and Reel Families, Free Family Movie Screenings, beginning at noon. Together, these programs create a seamless day of activities centered on creativity, community, and family-friendly fun.

“The Alliance Morning Market allows us to bring together so many of the things our community loves, local artists, creative experiences for kids, live entertainment, and time spent together,” said Alliance representative and organizer, Cat Flo. “It’s more than a market; it’s a full morning and afternoon of connection.”

Admission to the Alliance Morning Market and all accompanying activities is free. While gallery admission is always free, a $5 suggested donation helps support the Alliance’s mission to keep arts programming accessible and affordable.

Event: Alliance Morning Market, Indoors & Outdoors

Date: Every Third Saturday  Time: 9am–1pm

Includes: Local Vendors | Live Entertainment | Family ArtLab |  Free Family Movie

For more information about the Alliance Morning Market or other Alliance programs, visit ArtInLee.org or call 239-939-2787. For vending opportunities contact Cat@artinlee.org.

Throughout the series, you’ll build skills step by step — practicing brush control, double-loading techniques, blending, highlights, and shadow work — before applying your knowledge to design and completing your own decorative tray. event.title: Just Make
event.description:
You already know how to do this.

You’ve been making marks your whole life. In the margins of notebooks. On napkins. On the back of envelopes while you were thinking about something else entirely.

That impulse — the one that moves the pen before you decide to — is the most honest creative act you have. It’s also the one most people spend their entire lives dismissing.

Just Make is a one-day mixed-media workshop that gives that impulse a canvas, some paint, a pair of scissors, and permission.

We start fast. Marks get made before the critic wakes up. Paper gets torn. Things get glued in places that don’t make sense yet. Decisions happen at the speed of instinct — which is exactly the right speed for this.

Then something shifts.

The eye takes over. Composition emerges. You slow down and discover you’ve already made something worth finishing. The pieces were always going to go where they went.

You’ll leave with finished work on two surfaces — a canvas and a glass-mounted piece called a Slide — and the unsettling realization that you could have been doing this all along.

All primary materials provided. No experience necessary. No plan required.

Just show up.

Just make.

event.title: Step By Step Batik: Sunflower
event.description:
Explore the Art of Wax and Watercolor with a Fabric-Like Finish

If you’re looking for a unique and immersive art experience, this full-day workshop is not to be missed. Inspired by the traditional Indonesian technique of Batik, you’ll create a stunning layered painting using melted wax, watercolor, and Ginwashi rice paper — known for its beautiful translucent texture.

Guided by your instructor, you’ll work with multiple templates and learn how to build up color and design using wax-resist methods. The result is a one-of-a-kind painting with the look and feel of delicate, hand-dyed fabric. This class is perfect for beginners and seasoned artists alike who are eager to try something new.

A break will be taken for lunch on your own. Limited to just 6 participants to ensure plenty of individual instruction.


All supplies are provided

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet
event.description:
In this fun and relaxed four-week series, you’ll discover the building blocks of crochet while creating a beginner-friendly fall pumpkin. This class is designed for anyone who has wanted to learn to crochet, no prior experience required.

We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together.

Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own.

Supplies needed:

  • 5mm or 5.5mm crochet hook
  • Medium weight acrylic yarn
    • Body: orange, rust, cream, and other lighter fall themed colors (pick one)
    • Stem: brown and green (pick one)

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Prometheus Bound-Waldorf Inspired Story Class (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
In Prometheus Bound, students encounter the story of Prometheus and Epimetheus through oral narration, chalkboard drawing, discussion, and the creation of their own Main Lesson Books.
Their Main Lesson Books will be created from their own understanding and interpretation of the story rather than by simply copying the teacher’s work. Through writing, drawing, and bookmaking, students will develop a personal record of the myth while engaging its imagery, characters, and ideas in a distinctly Waldorf-inspired way.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Wise Humans (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
A Waldorf-Inspired Philosophy II Class

Building on the philosophical exploration begun in Philosophy I, Wise Humans takes students further into the strange problems, thought experiments, paradoxes, and ideas philosophers have used to investigate reality, knowledge, reason, and the human experience. Through storytelling, conversation, philosophical puzzles, and Waldorf-inspired Main Lesson Book work, students will encounter problems designed not simply to be solved, but to complicate what initially seems obvious. Students will consider questions of stability and change, the limits of knowledge, consciousness and perception, rational choice, time, meaning, and the peculiar difficulties that arise when apparently reasonable ideas collide.
The class emphasizes philosophical exploration rather than arriving at prescribed conclusions. Students will practice following an argument, noticing assumptions, considering competing possibilities, and becoming comfortable with questions that remain genuinely unsettled.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: What Is…Art? (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Rather than beginning with definitions, students will encounter objects, ideas, provocations, and philosophical problems that complicate the boundary between art and everything else.
The goal of the class is to not create art. Instead, students will attempt to understand art by testing its boundaries—asking what can be removed, changed, ignored, or rejected before something stops being art at all.

There may not be an answer. That’s the point.

 

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Wisdom Without the Hemlock-Arts/Philosophy Class II (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Wisdom without the Hemlock is a four-week arts and philosophy workshop built around the spirit of Socratic inquiry. Through Socrates, the Sophists, the Presocratics, dialogue, and philosophical problems, students will examine certainty, knowledge, and the nature of reality. Rather than memorizing a history of philosophy, students will practice questioning assumptions, following arguments, and thinking carefully, all while cultivating curiosity and wonder.

Know that you don’t know, so never stop asking.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Contemporary Painting with Terry Lynn
event.description:
Unlock your creativity in this engaging weekly painting class with beloved artist and instructor, Terry Lynn Spry! Designed for all skill levels—from beginners to seasoned professionals—this class allows students to work at their own pace with their preferred subject and medium.

Explore a wide range of painting styles, from realism to abstract, while deepening your understanding of portraiture, color control, composition, value studies, and drawing techniques. With personalized guidance and a supportive environment, you’ll refine your skills and develop your artistic voice.

Choose the best time of day for you:

Afternoon- 1pm-4pm

Evening- 6:30pm-9pm

event.title: Drop In with Terry Lynn (All Levels)
event.description:
Interested in taking a class with beloved Instructor Terry Lynn, but not sure you can make all the sessions? Wanting to try painting, but a little worried the class might be “over your head”? Then this is your big opportunity! Drop in and try one of Terry Lynn’s painting classes – Painting with Terry Lynn AM, Painting with Terry Lynn PM or Painting Studio with Terry Lynn – whichever time and whatever Tuesday works best for you!

Students have the choice to bring in a painting they’ve been working on. Or they can take a color class, drawing class or choose something from the instructor’s materials.

You may bring your own supplies (check supply list from Tuesday class) or purchase supply kit from the instructor for $20.

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: The Tempest: An Arts Encounter with Shakespeare’s The Tempest (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
The Tempest is a four-week arts and literature class for ages 13+ centered on the journey of Prospero as he confronts power, control, forgiveness, and the question of how to act once one possesses knowledge and agency. Each class begins with discussion and clarification of the assigned portion of the play. Students will examine Prospero’s changing relationship to the island, to the people
around him, and to his own power. In the second hour, students will create a landscape painting that represents where they understand Prospero to be at that point in his journey, drawing loosely on the compositional tradition of Taoist landscape painting. Over the course of the class, the three paintings will form a visual record of Prospero’s movement through the play. In the final session, the panels will be assembled into a triptych chronicling that journey.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Group Ukulele Lessons
event.description:
Strum, sing, and connect through music in this fun, welcoming group ukulele class for players of all levels. Whether you’re picking up an instrument for the first time or returning after a break, Amy Noel Walters will guide you through essential rhythm, chords, and technique in a way that’s supportive, creative, and confidence-building.

Each class blends hands-on practice with clear, easy-to-follow instruction, helping you build a strong musical foundation while exploring songs you love. You’ll also discover simple ways to incorporate breath, mindfulness, and body awareness into your playing, making music not just something you play, but something you feel. Bring your instrument, your curiosity, and a smile because making music is better together.

What to bring: Ukulele, tuner, water, and a notebook

Supply fee of $15 due directly to the Instructor


Single-class options available during the registration process. $30/members $35/non-members

event.title: Advanced Drawing for Tweens and Teens (Ages11-16)
event.description:
Drawing by Emily, age 11

Discover the skills to draw with greater confidence and realism! If you’ve ever wanted to improve your drawing abilities, this class will teach you how to truly see your subject rather than simply draw what you think it looks like. Through a series of guided exercises, you’ll learn techniques that help train your eye to recognize proportion, shape, value, and light.

Experiment with a variety of drawing materials, including charcoal pencils, compressed charcoal, and other black-and-white media, while building your skills through a range of subjects. You’ll draw still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models, developing the ability to capture light, shadow, depth, and form with greater accuracy.

Supplies Needed: 

  • 2 Charcoal Pencils, 6B extra soft
  • 2 White charcoal pencils OR White Compressed Charcoal
  • Pencil sharpener
  • Kneaded eraser

Paper provided

event.title: Zentangle for the Seasons
event.description:
Discover the Art of Zentangle: A Creative Journey Through the Seasons
Unwind and unlock your inner artist with Zentangle—a simple, meditative method of drawing beautiful patterns one step at a time. Perfect for beginners, this class starts with the foundational techniques and gradually builds your confidence and creativity. Each week, you’ll create unique seasonal artworks that reflect the time of year, combining relaxation with artistic expression. No prior experience needed—just a willingness to explore, create, and enjoy the process!

Supplies provided for a $10 fee due directly to the Instructor

event.title: Fine Art Acrylics with Marilyn Hedlund
event.description:
Join artist Marilyn Hedlund for a dynamic, critique-based class designed to inspire artists of all levels. Each session begins and ends with lively group critiques where ideas, techniques, and feedback are shared freely in a supportive environment.

Between critiques, you’ll work at your own station and pace, developing your artwork with personalized, one-on-one guidance from Marilyn. Expect to be challenged and inspired through stimulating discussions, creative assignments, and lecture/demos on essential topics like composition, form, color, and contrast.

This is more than a class—it’s a creative community where fresh ideas, constructive critique, and artistic growth go hand in hand.

event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description:
“Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.”

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

Topics include:

  • Gesture drawing fundamentals

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective

  • Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution

  • Differentiating core and cast shadows

  • Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy

Whether you’re just starting or refining your figure drawing skills, Francesco’s instruction will help you grow with clarity and confidence.

Supplies Needed:

* 2 Charcoal pencils 2B
* 1 White plastic eraser
* 1 Kneaded eraser
* 1 18″x 24″ Newsprint pad – 100 sheet
* Blending stumps assorted sizes 4 pc.
* No oils, solvent or fixatives are allowed in the class

event.title: Hula Dance (Ages 3-12)
event.description:
Experience the spirit and rhythm of the Pacific Islands in Hula with Marliss! This dynamic class introduces students to the traditional styles of Hawaiian, Tahitian, Māori, and Samoan dance. With a focus on both technique and cultural appreciation, students will learn the foundations of each style while mastering vibrant performance dances and songs.

Throughout the year, students will have the opportunity to showcase their skills and celebrate Polynesian culture at 3-4 community performances. Costumes are required for performances and are provided at a minimal cost.

Come dance, learn, and connect with the rich traditions of Polynesia in a fun and supportive environment!

NO CLASS ON 11/11 (Veteran’s Day) OR 11/25 (Thanksgiving Break)

event.description:
Now on Wednesday evenings 6-9pm AND Sunday afternoons 1-4pm!

Drop in, settle in, and draw! Life Drawing Lounge is a relaxed, non-instructed life drawing session featuring a nude model in one extended pose. Designed for artists of all levels with some basic life drawing experience, this is an opportunity to practice, experiment, and develop your skills in a casual, welcoming environment.

Enjoy music, light conversation, and the freedom to work at your own pace. Artists are encouraged to bring and use the medium of their choice.

$20 at the door
No instruction provided

event.title: Mend & Make New
event.description: Mend & Make New is a six‑week creative repair course that teaches students how to refresh, reinforce, and reimagine their clothing using both subtle and expressive techniques. Through invisible mending, visible patchwork, embroidery, darning, and hybrid redesign, students learn how to assess damage, choose the right materials, and build repairs that are both durable and personal. The class blends practical skill‑building with organic, discovery‑based learning while encouraging students to explore materials, experiment with stitches, and find their own style of repair. By the end of the series, each student completes a final project that combines multiple techniques and celebrates the character of well‑loved garments.

event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description:
You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter?

With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work.

Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections.

We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results.

This class is designed for everyone from the weekend photographer looking to sharpen their skills to semi-professional photographers and local realtors who want to create more polished, compelling images for their work.

Bring your questions and curiosity and leave with new tools and techniques to take your photography to the next level.

event.title: Master the Comma Stroke with Pat Smelkoff
event.description:
Discover the beauty of movement and rhythm in this engaging Comma workshop. In this hands-on class, you’ll learn how to use the expressive “comma” brushstroke to build texture, depth, and flow within your artwork. This versatile technique allows you to create everything from soft florals to dynamic landscapes using simple, repeated strokes.

With step-by-step guidance, you’ll explore brush control, layering, and composition while developing a style that feels both intuitive and meditative. Perfect for all skill levels, this class offers a relaxing, process-driven approach to painting, and a fresh technique you can carry into all your future work.

All supplies provided. This is a process driven workshop; you’ll leave with knowledge about the process, not a completed painting.

event.title: Art Without Rules: Teen MultiMedia Space (Age 13-18)

Each week introduces a new theme, artist, or source of inspiration, paired with guided mini-lessons that spark ideas and expand creative skills. Students will have the freedom to explore painting, drawing, mixed media, and more—while also continuing to develop personal projects over time.

This class balances structure with creative freedom, helping teens strengthen foundational skills, discover new mediums, and grow as artists in a supportive, inspiring environment. Single sessions available for $25/member, attend one session, or all 5!

event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description:
Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter.

Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings.

By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently.

For the first 2 classes, we will be limiting our palette to black and white.

event.title: Drawing Fundamentals (Ages 16+)
event.description:
Discover the joy of drawing in this inspiring 7-week course designed for artists of every skill level. Whether you’re a complete beginner who thinks you can’t draw or an experienced artist looking to refresh your skills and see your work in a new way, this class offers a supportive and engaging environment to grow.

Through guided exercises and personalized instruction, students will build confidence while developing essential drawing techniques, including observation, proportion, composition, value, and line quality. Working from a variety of subjects—including still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin drawing what is actually in front of you. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation of accurate, expressive, and confident drawing.

By the end of the seven weeks, you’ll have a stronger understanding of the fundamentals, improved observational skills, and the confidence to continue your artistic journey with a fresh perspective.

event.title: Get Hooked: An Introduction to Crochet
event.description:
In this fun and relaxed four-week series, you’ll discover the building blocks of crochet while creating a beginner-friendly fall pumpkin. This class is designed for anyone who has wanted to learn to crochet, no prior experience required.

We’ll begin with the fundamentals, including yarn and hook basics, how to hold your materials, tension control, and the essential crochet techniques you’ll need to get started. You’ll learn how to create a slip knot and chain before progressing to basic crochet stitches as we work through the project together.

Each session we’ll build on the previous weeks, giving you plenty of time to practice, ask questions, and receive hands on guidance along the way. By the end of the series, you’ll have completed your fall pumpkin and gained a foundation of skills you can continue to build on as you explore crochet on your own.

event.description:
In Prometheus Bound, students encounter the story of Prometheus and Epimetheus through oral narration, chalkboard drawing, discussion, and the creation of their own Main Lesson Books.
Their Main Lesson Books will be created from their own understanding and interpretation of the story rather than by simply copying the teacher’s work. Through writing, drawing, and bookmaking, students will develop a personal record of the myth while engaging its imagery, characters, and ideas in a distinctly Waldorf-inspired way.

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Wise Humans (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
A Waldorf-Inspired Philosophy II Class

Building on the philosophical exploration begun in Philosophy I, Wise Humans takes students further into the strange problems, thought experiments, paradoxes, and ideas philosophers have used to investigate reality, knowledge, reason, and the human experience. Through storytelling, conversation, philosophical puzzles, and Waldorf-inspired Main Lesson Book work, students will encounter problems designed not simply to be solved, but to complicate what initially seems obvious. Students will consider questions of stability and change, the limits of knowledge, consciousness and perception, rational choice, time, meaning, and the peculiar difficulties that arise when apparently reasonable ideas collide.
The class emphasizes philosophical exploration rather than arriving at prescribed conclusions. Students will practice following an argument, noticing assumptions, considering competing possibilities, and becoming comfortable with questions that remain genuinely unsettled.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: What Is…Art? (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Rather than beginning with definitions, students will encounter objects, ideas, provocations, and philosophical problems that complicate the boundary between art and everything else.
The goal of the class is to not create art. Instead, students will attempt to understand art by testing its boundaries—asking what can be removed, changed, ignored, or rejected before something stops being art at all.

There may not be an answer. That’s the point.

 

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Wisdom Without the Hemlock-Arts/Philosophy Class II (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Wisdom without the Hemlock is a four-week arts and philosophy workshop built around the spirit of Socratic inquiry. Through Socrates, the Sophists, the Presocratics, dialogue, and philosophical problems, students will examine certainty, knowledge, and the nature of reality. Rather than memorizing a history of philosophy, students will practice questioning assumptions, following arguments, and thinking carefully, all while cultivating curiosity and wonder.

Know that you don’t know, so never stop asking.

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: The Tempest: An Arts Encounter with Shakespeare’s The Tempest (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
The Tempest is a four-week arts and literature class for ages 13+ centered on the journey of Prospero as he confronts power, control, forgiveness, and the question of how to act once one possesses knowledge and agency. Each class begins with discussion and clarification of the assigned portion of the play. Students will examine Prospero’s changing relationship to the island, to the people
around him, and to his own power. In the second hour, students will create a landscape painting that represents where they understand Prospero to be at that point in his journey, drawing loosely on the compositional tradition of Taoist landscape painting. Over the course of the class, the three paintings will form a visual record of Prospero’s movement through the play. In the final session, the panels will be assembled into a triptych chronicling that journey.

event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description:

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

  • Gesture drawing fundamentals

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective

  • Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution

  • Differentiating core and cast shadows

  • Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy

Whether you’re just starting or refining your figure drawing skills, Francesco’s instruction will help you grow with clarity and confidence.

event.title: Picture Perfect: Exploring Photo Editing Techniques
event.description:
You already take great photos with your camera or cell phone, but what happens after you press the shutter?

With endless tutorials, YouTube videos, and AI tools at our fingertips, learning photo editing has never been more accessible. But there’s still tremendous value in sitting down with an experienced photographer who can help you understand not just how to edit, but why certain techniques work.

Led by digital lab instructor and photographer Robert Ahrens, this session explores the evolving world of digital photo editing, from traditional editing techniques to the newest AI-powered tools found in today’s software and online platforms. Learn how to improve your images, streamline your editing workflow, and make thoughtful creative choices rather than simply relying on automatic corrections.

We’ll also look at what you can do before you even press the shutter to give yourself a better image to work with later. Whether you’re photographing Florida wildlife, beaches, architecture, or our spectacular sunrises and sunsets, understanding the fundamentals of exposure, composition, resolution, and file quality can make a significant difference in your final results.

This class is designed for everyone from the weekend photographer looking to sharpen their skills to semi-professional photographers and local realtors who want to create more polished, compelling images for their work.

Bring your questions and curiosity and leave with new tools and techniques to take your photography to the next level.

Inspired by the beautifully hand-painted metal trays of Zhostovo painting, students will learn the signature “Russian Stroke” method used to create lush, dimensional floral designs set against rich, dark backgrounds.

Throughout the series, you’ll build skills step by step — practicing brush control, double-loading techniques, blending, highlights, and shadow work — before applying your knowledge to design and completing your own decorative tray. Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings.

By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently.

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Wise Humans (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
A Waldorf-Inspired Philosophy II Class

Building on the philosophical exploration begun in Philosophy I, Wise Humans takes students further into the strange problems, thought experiments, paradoxes, and ideas philosophers have used to investigate reality, knowledge, reason, and the human experience. Through storytelling, conversation, philosophical puzzles, and Waldorf-inspired Main Lesson Book work, students will encounter problems designed not simply to be solved, but to complicate what initially seems obvious. Students will consider questions of stability and change, the limits of knowledge, consciousness and perception, rational choice, time, meaning, and the peculiar difficulties that arise when apparently reasonable ideas collide.
The class emphasizes philosophical exploration rather than arriving at prescribed conclusions. Students will practice following an argument, noticing assumptions, considering competing possibilities, and becoming comfortable with questions that remain genuinely unsettled.

STEP UP students – follow this link to register:http://www.anthrogenics.com/general-4

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: What Is…Art? (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Rather than beginning with definitions, students will encounter objects, ideas, provocations, and philosophical problems that complicate the boundary between art and everything else.
The goal of the class is to not create art. Instead, students will attempt to understand art by testing its boundaries—asking what can be removed, changed, ignored, or rejected before something stops being art at all.

There may not be an answer. That’s the point.

Through Socrates, the Sophists, the Presocratics, dialogue, and philosophical problems, students will examine certainty, knowledge, and the nature of reality. Rather than memorizing a history of philosophy, students will practice questioning assumptions, following arguments, and thinking carefully, all while cultivating curiosity and wonder.

Each class begins with discussion and clarification of the assigned portion of the play. Students will examine Prospero’s changing relationship to the island, to the people

event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description:
“Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.”

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution

event.title: Shoot, Edit, Create: Unlocking the Art of Video
event.description:
Video has never been more accessible. What once required expensive cameras and complicated equipment can now be done with the device in your pocket. Today’s phones and digital cameras make it easy to capture high-quality video—and even offer basic editing tools right at your fingertips.

But creating a truly engaging video takes more than simply pressing record.

Join digital lab instructor Robert Ahrens for an approachable introduction to the fundamentals of shooting and editing video. Whether you’re using a smartphone, DSLR, or another digital camera, learn what to consider before you start recording and how those choices can make editing easier and your finished video stronger.

We’ll explore important basics such as frame rate (FPS), resolution, transferring video from your phone or camera to a computer, and navigating the video editing timeline. You’ll also learn how to create smooth transitions, add music, improve audio quality, and bring your clips together into a polished finished project.

We’ll take a look at how AI is changing the world of video creation and editing, too. While automated tools can be helpful, understanding the fundamentals gives you greater creative control and helps you make better decisions about when—and how—to use them.

No matter what editing software you choose, there is a learning curve. This class will give you a practical foundation and the confidence to begin experimenting with your own projects.

The skills you learn can be applied to everything from family memories and travel videos to real estate showcases, product demonstrations, and social media content.

Whether you’re completely new to video or have been shooting for years, come discover how to turn your footage into something worth watching.

“Let’s build a happy little cloud. Let’s build some happy little trees.” – Bob Ross
Join Mathew Halstead, CRI of Lazy Painter Brushworks, for a classic Bob Ross painting workshop with friends at the Alliance. event.description:
Step into a creative space where experimentation is encouraged and there’s no single “right” way to make art. In this ongoing studio-style class, teens will explore a wide range of materials and techniques while building confidence in their artistic voice.

Foulds Theater Gallery

Night Swim
by Zan Lombardo

“For viewers who want to enjoy this art installation on a surface level, imagine standing on a dock at night, looking down at fish swimming up to underwater lights.

For viewers who want to dive deeper into understanding the source of this imagery, know that my daily awareness swings widely between the wild beauty of our world and sadness about the way we treat it. My original plan for this installation was to create a winding labyrinth of continuous scrolls filled with beauty and despair that alternated at every turn. However, I soon discovered that I did not have the wherewithal to focus on, much less paint, despair. I have spent my adult life aligned with spiritual communities that gather together to receive the light, then go into the world, greeting everyone with that light. I will continue to behave artistically in this way.
Greetings to you all as you walk these light-filled paths. Move forward. Turn right and left. Look front and back. Be fascinated by the seeming chaos and know that it is blessed. Join in the movement toward the light. Come in to remember that you are the place where creation is working itself out, and as Jim Koopman said, have confidence in the river that runs clean beneath life’s storms.
The winding labyrinth was reimagined into forward paths leading viewers to physical and aesthetic sustenance at the bar and theater. The continuous scrolls have been divided into enough sections for everyone who wants to be encouraged about the wild beauty of our world and reminded to treat it as such.”

by the students of Life Drawing Lounge and Instructed Life Drawing

From guided instruction to independent practice, these works reflect the unique approaches of each class. Life Drawing Lounge offers a relaxed, uninstructed studio environment where artists develop their skills through extended poses and personal exploration in the medium of their choice under the guidance of artist Juli Bobman.

Together, these drawings demonstrate the enduring value of life drawing as both a foundational artistic practice and a deeply personal form of expression.

Guided by the instructor, participants will then apply these techniques to their own makeup, learning how to choose and blend colors that best complement their complexion and features.

Whether you’re new to makeup or looking to refine your skills, this class will give you practical knowledge you can use every day. All supplies are provided, including professional makeup products and materials needed for the workshop.

event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description:
Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter.

Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings.

By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently.

event.title: For the Love of Music, Vol. IV
event.description:
For the Love of Music, Vol. IV

Featuring Michelle Malone & Kelly Neff
Sunday, November 8 | 3:00–5:00 PM
Foulds Theatre at Alliance for the Arts

For the Love of Music returns for its fourth volume, bringing together award-winning singer-songwriters Michelle Malone and Kelly Neff for an intimate afternoon celebrating the songs, stories, and experiences that inspire the music.

More than a concert, For the Love of Music, Vol. IV invites audiences behind the songs to discover the heartbreaks, humor, triumphs, and unexpected moments that become music. Stripped down and personal, it’s a chance to experience music at its most authentic: one voice, one instrument, and one story at a time.

Michelle Malone

With a career spanning four decades, Michelle Malone is a fierce, genre-blending songwriter whose musical journey winds through folk, roots rock, Americana, country blues, and roadhouse rock. Known for emotionally direct songwriting, powerful vocals, and an unmistakable combination of grit and vulnerability, Malone has become an underground legend woven into the fabric of Georgia music.

Her remarkable career has included time as a “satellite member” of the Indigo Girls, performing as a guitarist with Kristian Bush of Sugarland, and appearing with the Atlanta Symphony alongside Gregg Allman and Chuck Leavell of the Rolling Stones. She has taken her music around the world and shared the road with an extraordinary range of performers—including ZZ Top and Ellen DeGeneres.

Across 17 studio albums, Malone has remained fiercely independent and committed to following the music wherever it takes her. Guitar World describes her as “equal parts badass guitar slinger and sweet songstress,” a combination that comes alive onstage through performances that are energetic, authentic, engaging, and soul-stirring.

In 2026, Malone celebrates an extraordinary milestone: 40 years of making music.

Kelly Neff

Joining Malone is Kelly Neff, an award-winning singer-songwriter whose rootsy blend of blues, folk, funk, and rock captures audiences from the first note.

A two-time Songwriter of the Year honoree from the Songwriters Showcase of America, Neff has opened for nationally recognized artists including Melissa Etheridge, Keb’ Mo’, and The Wallflowers. Her music combines soulful performance with rich storytelling, finding connection in moments of change, perseverance, and self-discovery.

Her most recent album, About Face, explores transformation and resilience—themes that take on even greater depth through Neff’s intimate live performances.

Together, Michelle Malone and Kelly Neff bring decades of songwriting, musicianship, and lived experience to the Foulds Theatre for an afternoon celebrating not only the finished song, but everything that happens before the first note is ever played.

A Waldorf-Inspired Philosophy II Class

Building on the philosophical exploration begun in Philosophy I, Wise Humans takes students further into the strange problems, thought experiments, paradoxes, and ideas philosophers have used to investigate reality, knowledge, reason, and the human experience. Through storytelling, conversation, philosophical puzzles, and Waldorf-inspired Main Lesson Book work, students will encounter problems designed not simply to be solved, but to complicate what initially seems obvious. Students will consider questions of stability and change, the limits of knowledge, consciousness and perception, rational choice, time, meaning, and the peculiar difficulties that arise when apparently reasonable ideas collide.
The class emphasizes philosophical exploration rather than arriving at prescribed conclusions. Students will practice following an argument, noticing assumptions, considering competing possibilities, and becoming comfortable with questions that remain genuinely unsettled.

During the first session, you’ll learn the 20-60-20 philosophy, study inspiring examples, and discuss techniques for expanding your creative eye. Between sessions, you’ll put these concepts into practice through a photography assignment. In the second session, you’ll share your work with the class, receive constructive feedback, and discuss how the 20-60-20 approach influenced your creative process.

Perfect for photographers who understand the basics and are ready to develop a stronger artistic voice, this workshop will help you create images that are not only technically successful but also uniquely your own.

event.title: Just Make
event.description:
You already know how to do this.

You’ve been making marks your whole life. In the margins of notebooks. On napkins. On the back of envelopes while you were thinking about something else entirely.

That impulse — the one that moves the pen before you decide to — is the most honest creative act you have. It’s also the one most people spend their entire lives dismissing.

Just Make is a one-day mixed-media workshop that gives that impulse a canvas, some paint, a pair of scissors, and permission.

We start fast. Marks get made before the critic wakes up. Paper gets torn. Things get glued in places that don’t make sense yet. Decisions happen at the speed of instinct — which is exactly the right speed for this.

Then something shifts.

The eye takes over. Composition emerges. You slow down and discover you’ve already made something worth finishing. The pieces were always going to go where they went.

You’ll leave with finished work on two surfaces — a canvas and a glass-mounted piece called a Slide — and the unsettling realization that you could have been doing this all along.

All primary materials provided. No experience necessary. No plan required.

Just show up.

Just make.

event.title: Instructed Life Drawing – Gestural & Structural Approach to the Figure (18+, Beginner to Advanced Level)
event.description:
“Students both beginning, intermediate and advanced can learn from Francesco’s excellent teaching methods, knowledge, humor, passion for the human form and all aspects of fine art. Students are fortunate to have an artist of his level as instructor.”

This class is ideal for students of all levels, from beginners to advanced. Rather than copying, you’ll learn to see and draw by interpreting the figure through gesture, form, and structure. Each session begins with a 30-minute demonstration by Francesco, followed by 2.5 hours of drawing from a live model. Individual guidance and feedback are available throughout the class.

Topics include:

  • Gesture drawing fundamentals

  • Building the figure with essential forms

  • Using contour lines and landmarks for volume and perspective

  • Understanding overlaps, foreshortening, and weight distribution

  • Differentiating core and cast shadows

  • Sighting techniques and simplified anatomy

Whether you’re just starting or refining your figure drawing skills, Francesco’s instruction will help you grow with clarity and confidence.

* 1 White plastic eraser
* 1 Kneaded eraser

event.title: Shoot, Edit, Create: Unlocking the Art of Video
event.description:
Video has never been more accessible. What once required expensive cameras and complicated equipment can now be done with the device in your pocket. Today’s phones and digital cameras make it easy to capture high-quality video—and even offer basic editing tools right at your fingertips.

But creating a truly engaging video takes more than simply pressing record.

Join digital lab instructor Robert Ahrens for an approachable introduction to the fundamentals of shooting and editing video. Whether you’re using a smartphone, DSLR, or another digital camera, learn what to consider before you start recording and how those choices can make editing easier and your finished video stronger.

We’ll explore important basics such as frame rate (FPS), resolution, transferring video from your phone or camera to a computer, and navigating the video editing timeline. You’ll also learn how to create smooth transitions, add music, improve audio quality, and bring your clips together into a polished finished project.

We’ll take a look at how AI is changing the world of video creation and editing, too. While automated tools can be helpful, understanding the fundamentals gives you greater creative control and helps you make better decisions about when—and how—to use them.

No matter what editing software you choose, there is a learning curve. This class will give you a practical foundation and the confidence to begin experimenting with your own projects.

The skills you learn can be applied to everything from family memories and travel videos to real estate showcases, product demonstrations, and social media content.

Whether you’re completely new to video or have been shooting for years, come discover how to turn your footage into something worth watching.

event.title: Conceptual Photography with Ron Timm
event.description:
Take your photography beyond snapshots and discover a more intentional, creative approach to making images. In this two-session workshop, you’ll explore the 20-60-20 Concept, a framework designed to strengthen both your technical skills and your artistic vision.

We’ll begin by examining the first 20%- creating solid, technically sound photographs that capture a scene. From there, you’ll move into the creative 60%, where you’ll experiment with composition, lighting, perspective, timing, and storytelling to create more compelling and meaningful images. Finally, you’ll challenge yourself in the last 20% by taking creative risks, breaking conventional rules, and exploring new ideas that push your photography beyond your comfort zone.

During the first session, you’ll learn the 20-60-20 philosophy, study inspiring examples, and discuss techniques for expanding your creative eye. Between sessions, you’ll put these concepts into practice through a photography assignment. In the second session, you’ll share your work with the class, receive constructive feedback, and discuss how the 20-60-20 approach influenced your creative process.

Perfect for photographers who understand the basics and are ready to develop a stronger artistic voice, this workshop will help you create images that are not only technically successful but also uniquely your own.

event.title: Alliance Morning Market
event.description:
The Alliance for the Arts has reimagined its community market experience with the launch of the Alliance Morning Artisan Market, a new monthly event held on the third Saturday of each month from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. The shift moves the Alliance’s former Wednesday night market to a vibrant Saturday morning gathering designed to bring families, artists, and the community together for a full day of creativity and connection.

The first Alliance Morning Market will take place Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026, on the Alliance’s 10-acre campus at 10091 McGregor Blvd. The market will feature a curated mix of artisans and vendors, local artists, and live entertainment, creating a welcoming, festival-style atmosphere for all ages.

By moving the market to Saturdays, the Alliance is aligning it with two popular free programs already offered on campus: Free Family ArtLabs, held from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., and Reel Families, Free Family Movie Screenings, beginning at noon. Together, these programs create a seamless day of activities centered on creativity, community, and family-friendly fun.

“The Alliance Morning Market allows us to bring together so many of the things our community loves, local artists, creative experiences for kids, live entertainment, and time spent together,” said Alliance representative and organizer, Cat Flo. “It’s more than a market; it’s a full morning and afternoon of connection.”

Admission to the Alliance Morning Market and all accompanying activities is free. While gallery admission is always free, a $5 suggested donation helps support the Alliance’s mission to keep arts programming accessible and affordable.

Event: Alliance Morning Market, Indoors & Outdoors

Date: Every Third Saturday  Time: 9am–1pm

Includes: Local Vendors | Live Entertainment | Family ArtLab |  Free Family Movie

For more information about the Alliance Morning Market or other Alliance programs, visit ArtInLee.org or call 239-939-2787. For vending opportunities contact Cat@artinlee.org.

event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description:
Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter.

Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings.

By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently.

For the first 2 classes, we will be limiting our palette to black and white.

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Myth, A Waldorf Inspired Intro to Mythology (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
Myth is a four-week Waldorf-inspired introduction to mythology for ages 9–11. Through stories drawn from the Greek, Indian, and Norse traditions, students will encounter myth as a way human beings have explored the natural world, suffering, change, wisdom, mortality, and the forces that shape human life.
The class moves through the story of Demeter and Persephone, Siddhartha’s encounter with the Four Sights, and the mythology of Odin. Storytelling, discussion, drawing, and Main Lesson Book work will allow students to engage each tradition imaginatively while also beginning to recognize the symbols, patterns, and enduring human concerns that appear across cultures.
Rather than treating mythology as a collection of ancient stories to memorize, the class approaches myth as a living form of human meaning-making—one that brings together imagination, observation, art, culture, and some of humanity’s oldest attempts to understand its place in the world.

event.title: Shoot, Edit, Create: Unlocking the Art of Video
event.description:
Video has never been more accessible. What once required expensive cameras and complicated equipment can now be done with the device in your pocket. Today’s phones and digital cameras make it easy to capture high-quality video—and even offer basic editing tools right at your fingertips.

But creating a truly engaging video takes more than simply pressing record.

Join digital lab instructor Robert Ahrens for an approachable introduction to the fundamentals of shooting and editing video. Whether you’re using a smartphone, DSLR, or another digital camera, learn what to consider before you start recording and how those choices can make editing easier and your finished video stronger.

We’ll explore important basics such as frame rate (FPS), resolution, transferring video from your phone or camera to a computer, and navigating the video editing timeline. You’ll also learn how to create smooth transitions, add music, improve audio quality, and bring your clips together into a polished finished project.

We’ll take a look at how AI is changing the world of video creation and editing, too. While automated tools can be helpful, understanding the fundamentals gives you greater creative control and helps you make better decisions about when—and how—to use them.

No matter what editing software you choose, there is a learning curve. This class will give you a practical foundation and the confidence to begin experimenting with your own projects.

The skills you learn can be applied to everything from family memories and travel videos to real estate showcases, product demonstrations, and social media content.

Whether you’re completely new to video or have been shooting for years, come discover how to turn your footage into something worth watching.

Foulds Theater Gallery

Selected Works by Nicole Foran

“Geography of Substitution employs mixed media to construct a geography of substitution—places that stand in for other places I have lived, remembered, or imagined. I represent Iowa as Indiana, Florida as South Texas, Oklahoma as Saskatchewan. These are not attempts at deception so much as deliberate misalignments, where visual similarities—flat horizons, qualities of light, roadside architectures, vegetation—become convincing enough to hold the weight of memory, but never fully resolve into truth.

What interests me is the instability between recognition and dissonance. A landscape might feel familiar, yet small details resist certainty. These substitutions reveal how memory edits and compresses place, often prioritizing emotional coherence over factual accuracy. The work leans into a kind of false nostalgia—a longing for places that are already partial, displaced, or misremembered.

The project also responds to contemporary conditions of representation shaped by artificial intelligence and synthetic imagery. As AI-generated images increasingly blur distinctions between documentation and fabrication, these works examine how easily familiarity and authenticity can be constructed. Rather than hiding these slippages, I foreground them, using substitution to question the reliability of both memory and photographic evidence.

Drawing extends this process by slowing it down, allowing inaccuracies and distortions to accumulate through translation and repetition. Ultimately, the work is less about accurately depicting place and more about the unstable space between lived experience, memory, and mediated images.”

event.title: Drawing Fundamentals Ages 16+
event.description:
Discover the joy of drawing in this inspiring 7-week course designed for artists of every skill level. Whether you’re a complete beginner who thinks you can’t draw or an experienced artist looking to refresh your skills and see your work in a new way, this class offers a supportive and engaging environment to grow.

Through guided exercises and personalized instruction, students will build confidence while developing essential drawing techniques, including observation, proportion, composition, value, and line quality. Working from a variety of subjects—including still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin drawing what is actually in front of you. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation of accurate, expressive, and confident drawing.

By the end of the seven weeks, you’ll have a stronger understanding of the fundamentals, improved observational skills, and the confidence to continue your artistic journey with a fresh perspective.

Supplies:

  • 2 Charcoal Pencils, 6B extra soft
  • 2 White charcoal pencils OR White Compressed Charcoal
  • Pencil sharpener
  • Kneaded eraser

Paper provided

event.title: Step By Step Batik: Sea Turtle
event.description:
Explore the Art of Wax and Watercolor with a Fabric-Like Finish

If you’re looking for a unique and immersive art experience, this full-day workshop is not to be missed. Inspired by the traditional Indonesian technique of Batik, you’ll create a stunning layered painting using melted wax, watercolor, and Ginwashi rice paper — known for its beautiful translucent texture.

Guided by your instructor, you’ll work with multiple templates and learn how to build up color and design using wax-resist methods. The result is a one-of-a-kind painting with the look and feel of delicate, hand-dyed fabric. This class is perfect for beginners and seasoned artists alike who are eager to try something new.

A break will be taken for lunch on your own. Limited to just 6 participants to ensure plenty of individual instruction.


All supplies are provided

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Myth, A Waldorf Inspired Intro to Mythology (Ages 9-11)
event.description:
Myth is a four-week Waldorf-inspired introduction to mythology for ages 9–11. Through stories drawn from the Greek, Indian, and Norse traditions, students will encounter myth as a way human beings have explored the natural world, suffering, change, wisdom, mortality, and the forces that shape human life.
The class moves through the story of Demeter and Persephone, Siddhartha’s encounter with the Four Sights, and the mythology of Odin. Storytelling, discussion, drawing, and Main Lesson Book work will allow students to engage each tradition imaginatively while also beginning to recognize the symbols, patterns, and enduring human concerns that appear across cultures.
Rather than treating mythology as a collection of ancient stories to memorize, the class approaches myth as a living form of human meaning-making—one that brings together imagination, observation, art, culture, and some of humanity’s oldest attempts to understand its place in the world.

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: How ‘Bout Them Apples-Waldorf Inspired ares Exploration of William Tell (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
How ’Bout Them Apples is a four-week Waldorf-inspired literature study for students ages 13+ centered on Friedrich Schiller’s William Tell.
