Foulds Theater Gallery

Selected Works by Nicole Foran

“Geography of Substitution employs mixed media to construct a geography of substitution—places that stand in for other places I have lived, remembered, or imagined. I represent Iowa as Indiana, Florida as South Texas, Oklahoma as Saskatchewan. These are not attempts at deception so much as deliberate misalignments, where visual similarities—flat horizons, qualities of light, roadside architectures, vegetation—become convincing enough to hold the weight of memory, but never fully resolve into truth.

What interests me is the instability between recognition and dissonance. A landscape might feel familiar, yet small details resist certainty. These substitutions reveal how memory edits and compresses place, often prioritizing emotional coherence over factual accuracy. The work leans into a kind of false nostalgia—a longing for places that are already partial, displaced, or misremembered.

The project also responds to contemporary conditions of representation shaped by artificial intelligence and synthetic imagery. As AI-generated images increasingly blur distinctions between documentation and fabrication, these works examine how easily familiarity and authenticity can be constructed. Rather than hiding these slippages, I foreground them, using substitution to question the reliability of both memory and photographic evidence.

Drawing extends this process by slowing it down, allowing inaccuracies and distortions to accumulate through translation and repetition. Ultimately, the work is less about accurately depicting place and more about the unstable space between lived experience, memory, and mediated images.”

event.title: Homeschool Enrichment Series: Of Two Minds- Arts/Philosophy Class III for Teens (Ages 13-18)
event.description:
Of Two Minds is a four-week arts and philosophy class for ages 13+ exploring the relationship between the rational and irrational dimensions of human life. Using Beauty and the Beast, The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, and philosophy from leading thinkers , students will encounter the rational and irrational through story, discussion, and artistic work.
Rather than treating reason and irrationality as opposing forces, students will explore their coexistence in equilibrium and its consequences.

event.title: Ukulele Group Lessons
event.description:
Strum, sing, and connect through music in this fun, welcoming group ukulele class for players of all levels. Whether you’re picking up an instrument for the first time or returning after a break, Amy Noel Walters will guide you through essential rhythm, chords, and technique in a way that’s supportive, creative, and confidence-building.

Each class blends hands-on practice with clear, easy-to-follow instruction, helping you build a strong musical foundation while exploring songs you love. You’ll also discover simple ways to incorporate breath, mindfulness, and body awareness into your playing, making music not just something you play, but something you feel. Bring your instrument, your curiosity, and a smile because making music is better together.

What to bring: Ukulele, tuner, water, and a notebook

Supply fee of $15 due directly to the Instructor


Single-class options available during the registration process. $30/members $35/non-members

event.description:
Drawing by Emily, age 11

Discover the skills to draw with greater confidence and realism! If you’ve ever wanted to improve your drawing abilities, this class will teach you how to truly see your subject rather than simply draw what you think it looks like. Through a series of guided exercises, you’ll learn techniques that help train your eye to recognize proportion, shape, value, and light.

Experiment with a variety of drawing materials, including charcoal pencils, compressed charcoal, and other black-and-white media, while building your skills through a range of subjects. You’ll draw still lifes, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models, developing the ability to capture light, shadow, depth, and form with greater accuracy.

Unwind and unlock your inner artist with Zentangle—a simple, meditative method of drawing beautiful patterns one step at a time. Each week, you’ll create unique seasonal artworks that reflect the time of year, combining relaxation with artistic expression. event.description: If you’re looking for the perfect holiday gift, this is it.  After this 2 hour workshop you, a family member or a friend will learn how to film, produce and edit a mini-documentary about the family’s history, to be able to share with future generations to come.  Affordable equipment needed, creating a comfortable interview enviroment, a list of and chronology of questions to ask, and a simple blueprint to follow the project to completion, will be provided.  The results for any history lover can prove to be very rewarding.

event.description:

With a focus on both technique and cultural appreciation, students will learn the foundations of each style while mastering vibrant performance dances and songs.

Come dance, learn, and connect with the rich traditions of Polynesia in a fun and supportive environment!

event.description:
NO CLASS 11/26

Enjoy being creative with transparent watercolors. Linda Benson’s hands-on teaching technique allows you to create along with her in the classroom. Learn something new or refresh your skills. You will learn brush techniques, color theory, perspective, gradients, and composition. Each week is a new lesson complete with reference handouts. You will learn tricks that aren’t in the book and secrets for a successful painting.

  • Watercolor brushes: Round and flat assortment with 1 inch flat
  • 140 Lb. Watercolor paper or block 11×14 (Arches is good watercolor paper but Strathmore is OK if it is 140-pound stock)
  • Watercolor pallet tray with cover

  • Pencils

  • Carry bag
  • Pencil case
  • If you already have some supplies, bring in what you have and we will work with that. Linda will have some brushes and some supplies to share on the first day of class for beginners. Advanced students bring what you have.

event.title: Acrylic Painting with Pat Smelkoff: Beginning Metal Zhostovo Tray
event.description:
Discover the elegance and drama of the traditional Russian decorative technique known as Zhostovo in this multi-week painting series. Inspired by the beautifully hand-painted metal trays of Zhostovo painting, students will learn the signature “Russian Stroke” method used to create lush, dimensional floral designs set against rich, dark backgrounds.

Throughout the series, you’ll build skills step by step — practicing brush control, double-loading techniques, blending, highlights, and shadow work — before applying your knowledge to design and completing your own decorative tray. We’ll explore traditional compositions, color harmony, and the bold contrast that makes this style so striking.

Perfect for beginners ready to learn foundational stroke work as well as experienced painters wanting to expand their decorative painting repertoire. By the end of the course, you’ll leave with a beautifully painted tray and the confidence to continue exploring this timeless folk art tradition.

All supplies are provided

This class will meet twice- on 12/3 and 12/10

event.title: Oil Painting Basics
event.description:
Build confidence and develop your painting skills in this comprehensive 7-week oil painting course designed for both beginners and experienced artists. Whether you’re picking up a brush for the first time or looking to strengthen your technique, this class offers personalized instruction and guided exercises that will help you grow as a painter.

Students will explore the essential materials, techniques, and principles of oil painting, including color mixing, composition, value, light, and brushwork. Through a variety of subjects—including still life, landscapes, self-portraits, and live models—you’ll learn to move beyond drawing what you think you see and begin painting from direct observation. This shift from symbolic thinking to perceptual seeing is the foundation for creating more accurate, expressive, and compelling paintings.

By the end of the course, participants will have completed several original paintings, gained a solid understanding of oil painting fundamentals, and developed the confidence to continue painting independently.

For the first 2 classes, we will be limiting our palette to black and white.

event.title: Alliance Morning Market
event.description:
The Alliance for the Arts has reimagined its community market experience with the launch of the Alliance Morning Artisan Market, a new monthly event held on the third Saturday of each month from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. The shift moves the Alliance’s former Wednesday night market to a vibrant Saturday morning gathering designed to bring families, artists, and the community together for a full day of creativity and connection.

The first Alliance Morning Market will take place Saturday, Feb. 21, 2026, on the Alliance’s 10-acre campus at 10091 McGregor Blvd. The market will feature a curated mix of artisans and vendors, local artists, and live entertainment, creating a welcoming, festival-style atmosphere for all ages.

By moving the market to Saturdays, the Alliance is aligning it with two popular free programs already offered on campus: Free Family ArtLabs, held from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m., and Reel Families, Free Family Movie Screenings, beginning at noon. Together, these programs create a seamless day of activities centered on creativity, community, and family-friendly fun.

“The Alliance Morning Market allows us to bring together so many of the things our community loves, local artists, creative experiences for kids, live entertainment, and time spent together,” said Alliance representative and organizer, Cat Flo. “It’s more than a market; it’s a full morning and afternoon of connection.”

Admission to the Alliance Morning Market and all accompanying activities is free. While gallery admission is always free, a $5 suggested donation helps support the Alliance’s mission to keep arts programming accessible and affordable.

Event: Alliance Morning Market, Indoors & Outdoors

Date: Every Third Saturday  Time: 9am–1pm

Includes: Local Vendors | Live Entertainment | Family ArtLab |  Free Family Movie

For more information about the Alliance Morning Market or other Alliance programs, visit ArtInLee.org or call 239-939-2787. For vending opportunities contact Cat@artinlee.org.

event.description:
On Display: January 8 – 30
Opening Reception: January 8, 5:00-7:00 p.m.

 

Selected Works by Mikhail Gubin

​Mikhail Gubin was born in the Soviet Union in 1953. He studied at the Art and Technology College of Zagorsk, Moscow region, Russia. In 1989 Mikhail Gubin immigrated to the United State of America, and settled in New York. His multimedia practice includes Sculpture, Drawing, Painting, Collage, Photography, Video. Mikhail participated in 38 solo shows and over 200 group exhibitions in the United State and internationally, received multiple awards and praises, many reviews (The New York Times among many others). He has being awarded a 2014 NYFA Fellowship in the category of CRAFTS/SCULPTURE. A member of the Audubon Artists inc., the National Collage Society, Sculpture Guild of New York, Florida CraftArt Gallery.

_________________________________

 

 

Selected Works by Macús Alonso

Macus Alonso is an interdisciplinary artist from Vigo, Spain based in Chicago and Southwest Florida. Traveling throughout the world has greatly influenced her practice. She began experimenting with jewelry while living in West Africa and since then has expanded to textiles and sculpture. She is a process artist that draws inspiration from the wide range of materials she works with. She had the opportunity to work with a loom and since then has not stopped weaving. Macus received her Master of Studio Art at Northern Illinois University, Dekalb, IL and her Bachelors degree from the University of Illinois at Chicago. She was an artist resident at Chicago Art Department and has had her pieces on display at SOFA, Oliva Gallery, Woman Made Gallery, Compound Yellow, Hyde Park Art Center, Bridgeport Art Center, Olson Gallery and many other galleries.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Foulds Theater Gallery

Selected Works by Maikel Rivero Fernández

In this exhibit, we invite you to explore Maikel Rivero Fernández’s serenity and reflection. This body of monochromatic works transform familiar subjects into contemplative studies of light, form, and atmosphere. Motifs long associated with traditional still life and botanical imagery get reimagined through an exploratory, reductive process in which charcoal is layered and erased to create tonal shifts that reveal transient, dreamlike imagery. By limiting color, Rivero Hernandez’s works invite viewers to slow down and focus on texture and gesture through both presence and absence.

Rivero Hernandez’s work is grounded drawing while still embracing experimentation both in the medium and the subject, allowing recognizable forms to exist between realism and abstraction. This results in pieces that offer moments of contemplation while demonstrating that techniques can be renewed through material exploration to create images that are simultaneously timeless, intimate, and meditative.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Member Gallery

Terry Lynn’s Students’ Exhibition

This exhibition features original acrylic paintings created by students of Terry Lynn Spry’s painting class. The works reflect a vibrant, critique-driven studio environment where experimentation, thoughtful feedback, and individual growth are central. Guided by Terry Lynn’s one-on-one instruction and group discussions, students explore composition, color, form, and contrast, resulting in a diverse collection that showcases both technical development and personal artistic voice.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Featured Artworks: “Crucifixion” by Mikhail Gubin, Untitled Artwork by Macús Alonso, “Caminante, No Hay Camino / Traveler, There’s No Path” by Maikel Rivero Fernández, and Untitled Artwork by Jessi Dilich

Selected Works by Mikhail Gubin

​Mikhail Gubin was born in the Soviet Union in 1953. He studied at the Art and Technology College of Zagorsk, Moscow region, Russia. In 1989 Mikhail Gubin immigrated to the United State of America, and settled in New York. His multimedia practice includes Sculpture, Drawing, Painting, Collage, Photography, Video. Mikhail participated in 38 solo shows and over 200 group exhibitions in the United State and internationally, received multiple awards and praises, many reviews (The New York Times among many others). He has being awarded a 2014 NYFA Fellowship in the category of CRAFTS/SCULPTURE. A member of the Audubon Artists inc., the National Collage Society, Sculpture Guild of New York, Florida CraftArt Gallery.

_________________________________

 

 

Selected Works by Macús Alonso

Macus Alonso is an interdisciplinary artist from Vigo, Spain based in Chicago and Southwest Florida. Traveling throughout the world has greatly influenced her practice. She began experimenting with jewelry while living in West Africa and since then has expanded to textiles and sculpture. She is a process artist that draws inspiration from the wide range of materials she works with. She had the opportunity to work with a loom and since then has not stopped weaving. Macus received her Master of Studio Art at Northern Illinois University, Dekalb, IL and her Bachelors degree from the University of Illinois at Chicago. She was an artist resident at Chicago Art Department and has had her pieces on display at SOFA, Oliva Gallery, Woman Made Gallery, Compound Yellow, Hyde Park Art Center, Bridgeport Art Center, Olson Gallery and many other galleries.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Foulds Theater Gallery

Selected Works by Maikel Rivero Fernández

In this exhibit, we invite you to explore Maikel Rivero Fernández’s serenity and reflection. This body of monochromatic works transform familiar subjects into contemplative studies of light, form, and atmosphere. Motifs long associated with traditional still life and botanical imagery get reimagined through an exploratory, reductive process in which charcoal is layered and erased to create tonal shifts that reveal transient, dreamlike imagery. By limiting color, Rivero Hernandez’s works invite viewers to slow down and focus on texture and gesture through both presence and absence.

Rivero Hernandez’s work is grounded drawing while still embracing experimentation both in the medium and the subject, allowing recognizable forms to exist between realism and abstraction. This results in pieces that offer moments of contemplation while demonstrating that techniques can be renewed through material exploration to create images that are simultaneously timeless, intimate, and meditative.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Member Gallery

Terry Lynn’s Students’ Exhibition

This exhibition features original acrylic paintings created by students of Terry Lynn Spry’s painting class. The works reflect a vibrant, critique-driven studio environment where experimentation, thoughtful feedback, and individual growth are central. Guided by Terry Lynn’s one-on-one instruction and group discussions, students explore composition, color, form, and contrast, resulting in a diverse collection that showcases both technical development and personal artistic voice.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Featured Artworks: “Crucifixion” by Mikhail Gubin, Untitled Artwork by Macús Alonso, “Caminante, No Hay Camino / Traveler, There’s No Path” by Maikel Rivero Fernández, and Untitled Artwork by Jessi Dilich

event.title: February Galleries Opening Reception: Pat Jacoby Harris | Maria Mijares | Marilyn Hedlund’s Students
event.description:
On Display: February 5 – 27
Opening Reception: January 5, 5:00-7:00 p.m.

 

Pat Jacoby Harris
A Retrospective Exhibition

Patricia Jacoby Harris was born in Peekskill, NY, September 15, 1940, and grew up in this Hudson River Valley area, 40 miles north of New York City. She was an art major at Hendrick Hudson HS, Montrose, NY. In 1959, Jacoby Harris enrolled in SUNY College of Art Education, Buffalo, NY, and spent a semester in Sienna, Italy. Studies included fresco painting, sculpture, pottery, art history, and Italian culture. She lived in New York City during the 1960’s and has divided subsequent years between Buffalo and Peekskill. In Peekskill 1986-1997, she opened PJH Showroom Gallery and had a studio in The Dempsey Flatiron Building in Peekskill’s Downtown Historic District.

Jacoby Harris is currently living in Southwest Florida. She has exhibited widely in New York State, Pennsylvania, and the Western New York Area, receiving many awards and Best of Shows for her work.

Watercolors painted with unconventional techniques reach dimensions of between 4 to 6 feet. The brushstrokes and washes compose highly animated imagery using transparent colors and opaque gouaches. She also works in acrylics on canvas, board, and paper, but another favorite medium is colored pencils and sticks. This medium is also used in a nontraditional manner. Abstract imagery is heavily built up of layers of pigment and burnishing which results in a highly glossy and rich surface.

In recent years the linear signature of these abstract paintings have found expression in fiber crafts and “Specious Artifacts”. The expression is in the creation of strands of fiber made from reclaimed and unraveled wools, mohairs, linens, cottons, silks, and acrylics of sweaters that are from all over the world. Hundreds of artifacts (mostly hats) have been sold at stores in Buffalo and New York City. Jacoby Harris is a longtime member of The Buffalo Society of Artists and has exhibited in many of their juried shows.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Foulds Theater Gallery

Selected Works by Maria Mijares

Maria Mijares is a contemporary realist painter who focuses on producing rich visual narratives through meticulous encapsulations of her lived experience. She draws on the connections of her life in New York, New Jersey, and her family’s ancestral Santander, Spain to create artworks that highlight the details of her outdoor life. She refers to this intense care for detail as “psychedelic precision.” Her work exists as representations of identity, place, and memories while highlighting the simplicities of everyday life. Internationally exhibited and represented in numerous museum collections, Mijares brings together realism and storytelling in paintings that resonate through intimacy and contemplation.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Member Gallery

Marilyn Hedlund’s Students’ Exhibition

This exhibition features original acrylic paintings created by students of Marilyn Hedlund’s Fine Art Acrylics Class. The works reflect a vibrant, critique-driven studio environment where experimentation, thoughtful feedback, and individual growth are central. Guided by Marilyn’s one-on-one instruction and group discussions, students explore composition, color, form, and contrast, resulting in a diverse collection that showcases both technical development and personal artistic voice.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Featured Artworks: “First Panorama” by Pat Jacoby Harris, “Twilight Boats” by Maria Mijares, “Dreaming of Lavender Trees” by Vicki Baker

event.description:
On Display: March 5 – 27
Opening Reception: March 5, 5:00-7:00 p.m.

 

41st Annual All-Florida Exhibition

This annual show is the most anticipated of the year. As the name suggests, this exhibition features pieces created by artists working in a wide variety of media from all over the 65,000 square miles that make up Florida. The juried entries come together for an award-winning and exciting exhibition representing today’s contemporary Florida artists.

 

_____________________________________________________________

Foulds Theater Gallery

Selected Works by Leo Boisvert

Leo Boisvert is a contemporary eclectic painter and landscape/nature photographer based in Fort Myers, Florida. Originally from Bowie, Maryland, he developed his artistic foundation under the guidance of his father, Gerald Boisvert, a fledgling artist. He later deepened his knowledge through art theory and application classes at the University of Maryland.

Boisvert’s distinctive personal style is characterized by vibrant, colorful compositions that blend elements of Abstract, Post-Impressionism, Primitivism, and Synthetism. Employing single-point perspective, his paintings use flowing shapes, rich colors, and dynamic lines to evoke emotion and guide the viewer’s eye in continuous movement across the canvas. His work is influenced by his father, Gerald Boisvert, as well as iconic figures such as Keith Haring, Louis Rosemont, and Tristan Eaton. He works primarily in acrylic paint, often incorporating mixed media, while his photography spans both color and black-and-white formats. Boisvert views artistry as an innate calling rather than solely an academic pursuit. Though formally trained, he has refined his voice through hands-on experience, continuous self-study, trial and error, and close observation of master artists.

One of his paintings has been featured on a label for Rare Character Whiskey Company’s bourbon, and multiple works are currently on display at Craft Spirits Social in Bonita Springs, Florida. Boisvert’s art has been exhibited at various Alliance of the Arts shows and resides in private collections across the country through commissioned pieces for client homes.

South Fort Myers High School All Access Art Program is a collaborative effort between general education students and students with special needs. event.description:
Now on Wednesday evenings 6-9pm AND Sunday afternoons 1-4pm!

Drop in, settle in, and draw! Life Drawing Lounge is a relaxed, non-instructed life drawing session featuring a nude model in one extended pose. Designed for artists of all levels with some basic life drawing experience, this is an opportunity to practice, experiment, and develop your skills in a casual, welcoming environment.

Enjoy music, light conversation, and the freedom to work at your own pace. Artists are encouraged to bring and use the medium of their choice.

$20 at the door
No instruction provided
